claims.text: The initial alloy is a rapidly solidified, non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight HEA with density below 6 g/cm3.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous Mg distribution and a metastable single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
Thermal aging or annealing below the melting temperature enhances Mg diffusion in the metastable solid solution.
Enhanced Mg diffusion causes Mg segregation and phase separation during thermal aging.
Mg segregation produces discrete Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
The Mg-rich intermetallic compounds preferentially occur at grain boundaries or within the matrix.
Lightweight HEAs can contain a solid solution together with a minor ordered phase.
The temperature and composition range can affect whether candidate elements in a lightweight HEA form a solid solution.
Mg-rich intermetallic regions reduce the chemical and microstructural uniformity of the alloy.
Mg-rich intermetallic regions generate less protective and more heterogeneous oxide scales than the original metastable solid solution.
The heterogeneous oxide scales disrupt coherent aqueous-corrosion passivation.
The heterogeneous oxide scales reduce high-temperature oxidation protection.
Thermally aged samples will have higher corrosion rates and less uniform passivation than the initial rapidly solidified samples.
Thermally aged samples will develop thicker, more non-uniform, or less adherent oxide scales than the initial rapidly solidified samples.
The proposed evolution pathway applies within the studied Mg concentration range to lightweight HEAs with density below 6 g/cm3.
Large changes in composition or processing conditions may prevent the proposed evolution pathway.
